name: Lahanan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only classification refs (Kroeger 1998; Smith 2017 Borneo classification); no descriptive phonology found

sources.citation: Blust, Robert & Alexander D. Smith. 2014. A bibliography of the languages of Borneo (and Madagascar). Phillips, ME: Borneo Research Council.
sources.note: Bibliography: lists 'Lahanan (Melanau-Kajang; Sarawak; 350 in 1981)' but contains no descriptive entry (grammar/phonology) for Lahanan -- confirms none existed as of 2014.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2022 [print 2023]. Reconstructing non-contrastive stress in Austronesian and the role of the mora in stress shift, gemination and vowel shift. Diachronica 40(1): 111-152. doi:10.1075/dia.20032.smi
sources.note: Sister language Sekapan only (p. [26]): penultimate stress, shifted to the final syllable after an open penult with schwa (onset gemination). Lahanan is not mentioned anywhere.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A comprehensive classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. xxii+701 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Primary Lahanan field data (Sungai Asap; consultant Rainly Tigang). Sec. 2.3.1.1 'Kajang phonological evidence' pp. 93-97 gives PMP reflex tables for Sekapan/Kejaman/Lahanan; p. 99 'Kajang languages regularly geminate consonants after schwa.. In Kejaman, gemination surfaces as a glottal stop+consonant cluster'; sec. 3.5.1.1 pp. 341-343 gemination after schwa (Sekapan phonetic forms) and p. 343 'gemination after schwa is a broad feature of Austronesian stress'. The word 'stress' is never applied to Lahanan or to Kajang; no stress marks in Lahanan transcriptions. SILENT on Lahanan stress placem…

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian Languages (revised ed.). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Lahanan cited only for rightward rounding spread (tulwaŋ 'bone', p. ~620) and with '?' in Table 9.6 (final devoicing). Nothing on Lahanan stress.

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R. 2012. Melanau and the Languages of Central Sarawak. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-011. Dallas: SIL International. 100 pp.
sources.note: Comparative-lexical study; Lahanan forms from Rousseau's ABVD list and Urquhart 1955 used in cognate sets (p. 22 calls the Rousseau Lahanan list 'especially reliable'). No phonetic or prosodic description; a full-text search for stress/accent/penult yields nothing relevant. SILENT.

sources.citation: Alexander, Jennifer. 2006 [1993]. The Lahanan Longhouse. In James J. Fox (ed.), Inside Austronesian Houses, ch. 2, pp. 31-43. Canberra: ANU E Press. doi:10.22459/IA.09.2006.02
sources.note: Ethnography; no language or orthography note. SILENT.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1913. The Languages of Borneo. Sarawak Museum Journal 1(4): 1-196.
sources.note: Kajaman vocabulary and location note only; no Lahanan list; its single 'stress' remark concerns Mantangai Ngaju sentence stress. SILENT for Lahanan.
